{{Short description|German doctor and mathematician}}
[[File:Magnus Pegel.jpg|right|thumb|Magnus Pegel]]

'''Magnus Pegel''' (or '''Pegelius''' or '''Pegelow''') (15 May 1547 &ndash; 1619) was a [[German people|German]] doctor and [[mathematician]].<ref>{{citation | chapter-url = http://cpr.uni-rostock.de/metadata/cpr_professor_000000001101 | title = Catalogus Professorum Rostochiensium | chapter = Pegel, Magnus | postscript = <!--none--> }}</ref> Pegel was born in [[Rostock]] in Pomerania/Germany and was one of the first authors to write (in 1604) about the theory of [[blood transfusion]]s.<ref>{{citation | title = Studies in the history and method of science, Vol II | editor = Charles Singer | year = 1921 | author = F. J. Cole | chapter = The history of anatomical injections | postscript = <!--none-->}}</ref><ref>{{ Citation | title = The history and future of transfusion medicine | author = J Greenwalt | journal = Transfusion Today | issue = 23 | date = August 1995 | issn = 1015-3276 | postscript = <!--none-->}}</ref><ref>{{citation | title = Address in obstetrics diseases of women and children | author = [[Theophilus Parvin]] | journal = Transactions of the American Medical Association | publisher = American Medical Association | year = 1874 | postscript = <!--none-->}}</ref><ref>{{citation | title = Practical blood transfusion | year = 1970 |author1=Douglas W. Huestis |author2=Joseph R. Bove |author3=Shirley Busch | postscript = <!--none-->}}</ref>  He died at [[Stettin]].

== Works ==

* "Disputatio de peste"
* "Universi seu mundi Diatyposis"
* "Thesaurus rerum selectarum"
* "Aphorismi thesum selectarum"
